rv.q: As does Boye, who proves in two short hours she is a tragicomic force to be reckoned with.
This version of HAPPY DAYS is a must-see for Beckett fans and for anyone interested in exploring a modern theater classic.
This is not a story that everyone will enjoy.

cn.t: Kayla Boye proves equal to the demands of Beckett's notoriously difficult "summit part," delivering an effervescent performance that captures Winnie's curiosity and optimism amid the tragicomic futility of this challenging work.
